blindSummary:
This state/province recorded 3 killings of trans women and people of a locally established trans-feminine identity in 2025. Against a population of ~3.6 million the rate is approximately 0.83 per million per year — more than double the national rate of 0.38 per million. The state/province sits on an agricultural-expansion frontier, an area where the pattern that 68% of such killings fall outside the capitals makes small-town exposure relevant for a visitor travelling beyond the state's main city.

The elevated per-capita rate justifies a small deviation below the national average; the deviation is modest because 3 cases on a small population is statistically fragile and no qualitative incident, ordinance, or enforcement evidence was found beyond the national trans-advocacy association's count. Compared with a neighbouring state/province that recorded 5 killings on ~7.2 million people (rate ~6.9 per 10 million), this state/province's per-capita figure is actually higher, but its smaller absolute count and absence of corroborating detail justify a smaller deviation.
